citation.authors: Gálvez MV, Aguilera J, Leal M, et al

record.population: 25 volunteers (back skin); ancestry not given in the abstract. Sunscreens: ISO-standard SPF 16 and 63 and four commercial SPF 50 or 50+ products
record.design: Experiment: sunscreen and moisturising cream applied in different orders, measured by ultraviolet reflectance photography
record.finding: There were no significant differences in UV reflection when moisturising creams were applied before or after the sunscreens. The sunscreens themselves reduced the colour measure by 35% to 70%, showing real UV absorption. The authors conclude sunscreen effectiveness was not altered by concomitant moisturiser.
record.note: Small; measured UV reflectance, not sunburn or real-world protection; only non-sunscreen moisturising creams, not serums, acids or retinoids; funding not checked.
